candidate.answerReason: Each of the 6 entrance windows allows 5 different exit windows, giving 30 ways.

methods.label: Count choices for each entrance
methods.explanation:
First choose the entrance window, which can be any of the \(6\) windows. For each entrance, Georgie has \(5\) exit choices because he cannot leave through the window he entered. Every valid trip has exactly one entrance and one exit, so these choices include every trip exactly once. Reversing the entrance and exit gives a different trip. Thus there are
\[
6\cdot5=30
\]
ways, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
methods.levelReason: This is elementary counting of two successive choices, without permutation notation or formulas.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is counting pairings systematically without omissions or repetitions. The method groups trips by entrance and counts five exits in each group, using multiplication to combine equal group sizes.
